f.title: Commence ordered device postmarket surveillance within 15 months of FDA's order
f.statement: A device manufacturer that is ordered by FDA (the Secretary) to conduct postmarket surveillance under FD&C Act section 522 shall commence the surveillance not later than 15 months after the day on which the Secretary issues the order.
f.clause: Sec. 616, amending FD&C Act sec. 522(b)(1) Postmarket surveillance
f.applicability: Devices subject to a section 522 postmarket surveillance order (which, as amended, may be issued at the time of approval or clearance or at any time thereafter)
f.processes: Epidemiology / safety studies; Risk management & minimisation

f.title: Notify FDA of permanent discontinuance or meaningful supply interruption of life-saving drugs at least 6 months ahead
f.statement: A manufacturer of a drug that is life-supporting, life-sustaining, or intended for use in the prevention or treatment of a debilitating disease or condition (including drugs used in emergency medical care or during surgery), and that is not a radio pharmaceutical drug product or other product designated by the Secretary, shall notify the Secretary of a permanent discontinuance in the manufacture of the drug or an interruption of manufacture that is likely to lead to a meaningful disruption in the supply of the drug in the United States, and of the reasons for the discontinuance or interruption. The notice shall be submitted at least 6 months prior to the date of the discontinuance or interruption or, if that is not possible, as soon as practicable.
f.clause: Sec. 1001(a), FD&C Act sec. 506C(a)-(b) Discontinuance or interruption in the production of life-saving drugs
f.applicability: Life-supporting, life-sustaining drugs, or drugs intended for prevention or treatment of a debilitating disease or condition (including drugs used in emergency medical care or during surgery)
f.exceptions: Radio pharmaceutical drug products and any other product designated by the Secretary

f.title: Respond in writing within 30 calendar days to an FDA letter on failure to notify a discontinuance or interruption
f.statement: Not later than 30 calendar days after the Secretary issues a letter informing a person of a failure to submit the required discontinuance or interruption notification in accordance with the timing requirements, the person who receives the letter shall submit to the Secretary a written response setting forth the basis for noncompliance and providing the information required under subsection (a).
f.clause: Sec. 1001(a), FD&C Act sec. 506C(f) Failure to meet requirements
f.applicability: Drugs subject to the sec. 506C(a) notification requirement

f.title: Include in each REMS assessment an evaluation of whether each goal and element is being met
f.statement: A REMS assessment for a drug shall include, with respect to each goal included in the strategy, an assessment of the extent to which the approved strategy, including each element of the strategy, is meeting the goal or whether one or more goals or elements should be modified.
f.clause: Sec. 1132(a)(3), amending FD&C Act sec. 505-1(g)(3) REMS assessment content
f.applicability: Drugs with an approved risk evaluation and mitigation strategy (REMS)

f.title: Responsible person may propose a modification to an approved REMS at any time
f.statement: After the approval of a REMS by the Secretary, the responsible person may, at any time, submit to the Secretary a proposal to modify the approved strategy.
f.clause: Sec. 1132(a)(4), FD&C Act sec. 505-1(g)(4)(A) Modification on initiative of responsible person

f.title: Include an adequate rationale in a proposal to add, modify or remove REMS goals or elements
f.statement: A proposal to modify an approved REMS shall include an adequate rationale to support the proposed addition, modification, or removal of any goal or element of the strategy.
f.clause: Sec. 1132(a)(4), FD&C Act sec. 505-1(g)(4)(A) Modification on initiative of responsible person

f.title: FDA may require submission of a REMS modification proposal within 120 days or the time FDA specifies
f.statement: After approval of a REMS, FDA (the Secretary), in consultation with the offices described in sec. 505-1(c)(2), may at any time require the responsible person to submit a proposed modification to the strategy within 120 days or within such reasonable time as FDA specifies, if FDA determines that one or more goals or elements should be added, modified, or removed from the approved strategy to (i) ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh its risks or (ii) minimize the burden on the health care delivery system of complying with the strategy. Where FDA issues such a requirement, the proposed modification is due within 120 days or the time FDA specifies.
f.clause: Sec. 1132(a)(4), FD&C Act sec. 505-1(g)(4)(B) Modification on initiative of Secretary

f.title: Submit NDA, IND, ANDA and BLA submissions in the electronic format FDA specifies in guidance
f.statement: Beginning no earlier than 24 months after the issuance of a final guidance issued after public notice and opportunity for comment, submissions under subsection (b), (i), or (j) of FD&C Act section 505 or subsection (a) or (k) of Public Health Service Act section 351 shall be submitted in the electronic format specified in that guidance.
f.clause: Sec. 1136, FD&C Act sec. 745A(a)(1) Electronic format for submissions - drugs and biologics
f.applicability: Submissions under FD&C Act sec. 505(b), (i), (j) and PHS Act sec. 351(a), (k)
f.exceptions: The guidance may set criteria for waivers and exemptions; the subsection does not apply to submissions described in section 561
